category_title: Students who use overprotectiveness and aggression to control partners
student_description: This student struggles with controlling behavior, intense jealousy, and intimate violence rooted in past trauma and childhood abuse. When triggered by perceived flirting or feelings of inadequacy, he becomes defensive and physically acts out (e.g., banging doors). He uniquely requires gentle, discursive questioning to reframe cognitive distortions and link his current reactions to past experiences, as authoritative or clinical approaches trigger severe defensiveness.

criteria.rationale: Over time, the student needs a structured pathway to move from merely observing his triggers to actively practicing non-defensive responses.
criteria.check: The long-term plan includes a structured progression that starts with identifying problems and gradually shifts focus toward exploring and practicing alternative, non-defensive behaviors.

criteria.rationale: Because his behavioral issues stem from deep-seated physical and emotional abuse, one-on-one interviews alone are insufficient for sustained change.
criteria.check: The long-term plan incorporates multiple therapeutic modalities (e.g., group discussions, behavioral sports therapy, curriculum-based instruction) alongside targeted interviews.
